description: A QUOTED name resolves to ITSELF and to nothing else. The bare reference already did; three other lookups still FOLDED a quoted part before looking it up, so each of them ACCEPTED SQL a real account refuses - the direction that matters most. So the qualified reference is pinned with either part quoted and with an alias on either side, an ORDER BY key is pinned as a reference like any other, and WHERE, GROUP BY, an aggregate argument, a HAVING argument, a window ORDER BY key and a QUALIFY PARTITION BY key are all pinned the same way. The alias rules are the mirror image: a QUOTED alias answers to its own spelling only, never to the folded one, while an UNQUOTED alias answers to the folded name and never to a lower-case quoted one. The spellings that DO name the column still read, so the rule cannot have widened. And the ECHO has a rule of its own, measured spelling by spelling: a quoted name keeps its quotes only when it NEEDS them, so "Q", "A_B", "A1" and "$X" all echo bare while "qQ", "1A", "Abc" and "NO SUCH" keep theirs. Converted 1:1 from query/QuotedReferenceResolutionTest (now retired).

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE kw (a INT, b INT)
INSERT INTO kw VALUES (1, 2)
SELECT SUM("a") FROM kw
SELECT "a" + 1 FROM kw
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM kw GROUP BY a HAVING SUM("b") > 0
SELECT a, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "a") FROM kw
SELECT a FROM kw QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "a" ORDER BY a) = 1
SELECT MAX(a) FROM kw HAVING MAX("a") > 0
